prompt: Which statements are correct regarding the following commands executed on a Linux router? (Choose two.) `ip6tables -A FORWARD -s fe80::/64 -j DROP` and `ip6tables -A FORWARD -d fe80::/64 -j DROP`
choices: The rules disable packet forwarding because nodes always use `fe80::/64` addresses to identify routers in their routing tables
Both `ip6tables` commands complete without an error message or warning
Packets with source or destination addresses from `fe80::/64` will never occur in the FORWARD chain
The rules suppress any automatic configuration through router advertisements or DHCPv6
The second command returns an error because the affected network is already part of another rule
explanation: Both commands are accepted without error. Because `fe80::/64` is link-local, the rules also suppress autoconfiguration that relies on it, such as router advertisements and DHCPv6.
